item.title: Understanding Alphabet Learning in Kindergarten
item.description:
The alphabet is the foundation for reading, writing, and spelling success. In Kindergarten, students learn letter names, sounds, and letter combinations (graphemes) through explicit instruction that progresses from simple to more complex. Parents can help by reading with their child daily, using alphabet flash cards, playing matching games with uppercase and lowercase letters, and practicing sound identification games in the car.

item.description:

item.title: 3rd Grade State Testing Information
item.description:
3rd grade students will take the fall English Language Arts Ohio State Test on Wednesday, October 21st and Thursday, October 22nd, beginning at 9:30am. Parents are encouraged to write letters of encouragement for their children to read before testing and to avoid scheduling appointments on these mornings. A 3rd grade Pep Rally will be held Monday, October 19th, and students who do their best on the test will be invited to a Movie Party on Thursday, October 29th. Testing tips include: get plenty of rest, be on time, eat a good breakfast, relax and take a deep breath, and follow your teacher's directions.

item.title: PAX Good Behavior Game Program
item.description:
The PAX Good Behavior Game is a research-based classroom strategy that helps students make positive choices and collaborate with others. It promotes a calmer, more focused learning environment through kindness, teamwork, and respectful behavior.

The September and October 2026 calendars show daily PAX activities for students, including tasks like listening to classical music, creating PAX visions, helping others, expressing gratitude, and participating in themed days like National Read a Book Day and National Positivity Thinking Day.

item.title: September Attendance Awareness Month
item.description:
September is Attendance Awareness Month. Ohio defines chronic absenteeism as missing 10% of the year (both excused and unexcused absences), and this is calculated by hours missed, not just days—meaning tardies and early dismissals count. Families will receive monthly letters if their child reaches 10% or more absences. The school encourages families to be mindful of attendance and reach out if they need assistance.

item.title: School Health Guidelines: When to Stay Home
item.description:
Students should stay home if they have: fever of 100°F or higher, vomiting or diarrhea within 24 hours, undiagnosed rash with fever, active head lice, sore throat with fever/swollen glands/strep, eye infection with discharge, severe respiratory illness, or feel too sick to participate. Students can return when: fever-free for 24 hours without medicine, vomiting resolved overnight and can hold down food, diarrhea improved to no more than 2 accidents per 24 hours, rash cleared by doctor, lice treatment completed, 12-24 hours after antibiotics (for strep/eye infection), or respiratory symptoms improving for 24 hours and fever-free. Stay healthy by washing hands, covering coughs, and being kind.
